item.research_question: Can nanocrystalline high-entropy rare-earth hexaboride (HEReB6) ceramics be fabricated to achieve combined structural and functional performance, specifically high mechanical properties and superior thermionic emission, suitable for extreme environments?
item.material_system: (La0.25Ce0.25Nd0.25Eu0.25)B6 (HEReB6-1) and individual binary rare-earth hexaborides (LaB6, CeB6, NdB6, EuB6)
item.processing_route: Solid-state reaction of La2O3, CeO2, Nd2O3, Eu2O3, and NaBH4 at 1,373 K for 30 min to synthesize nanopowders; followed by high-pressure sintering of nanopowders at 6 GPa and 1,473–1,773 K for 5 min to fabricate bulk ceramics
item.test_conditions: Mechanical tests (Vickers hardness, fracture toughness) from room temperature to 1,073 K; electrical resistivity from 200 to 320 K; thermionic emission current density measured in vacuum (< 5 × 10−5 Pa) at 1,673 K, 1,773 K, and 1,873 K
key_findings: Relative density of 96.3 ± 2.2% achieved with a nanoscale grain size of 94 ± 28 nm at a sintering temperature of 1,673 K.
Vickers hardness of 23.4 ± 0.4 GPa and elastic modulus of 261 ± 13 GPa at room temperature, exceeding the average values of the four individual ReB6 samples (18.3 GPa and 232 GPa, respectively).
Fracture toughness of 3.0 ± 0.2 MPa•m1/2 at room temperature, slightly higher than the average of the four individual ReB6 samples (2.7 MPa•m1/2).
Electrical resistivity of HEReB6-1 was greater than the average value of the four individual ReB6 samples across the measured temperature range.
Maximum emission current density reached 48.3 A•cm−2 at 1,873 K, significantly higher than polycrystalline ReB6 samples.
Effective work function (Φe) of 2.83 eV at 1,873 K, which was slightly lower than the average values of the four individual ReB6 cathodes.
The (001) fiber texture was identified as the major texture orientation in the nanocrystalline microstructure.
item.mechanism: The superior mechanical properties are attributed to solid-solution and grain-refinement strengthening effects, along with nanoscale crack-deflection and grain-bridging toughening mechanisms. The high electrical resistivity results from exacerbated electron scattering due to severe lattice distortion. The remarkable thermionic emission performance is primarily attributed to the presence of the (001) fiber texture, which exposes surfaces with the lowest work function, and the contribution of d-orbital electrons from rare-earth elements (particularly Nd) to the conduction band.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The authors propose that this work will open up a new research field on HEReB6 ceramics with potential applications in thermionic emission cathodes.
quotes: The results showed that the samples possessed outstanding comprehensive mechanical properties and a high electrical resistivity from room temperature to high temperatures
For instance, the maximum emission current density reached 48.3 A•cm−2 at 1873 K.
Such superior performance makes the nanocrystalline HEReB6-1 ceramics highly suitable for potential applications in thermionic emission cathodes.
